speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: During this period, we mounted multiple public health responses that pushed us to new limits.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We faced a major economic challenge and fought to save lives and jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All of us adapted to different restrictions as the virus threat evolved.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Throughout these challenges, Singaporeans have rallied together and supported one another.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I want to express my deep appreciation to our stout-hearted healthcare workers who have been unwavering on the frontlines; as well as many others who have kept Singapore going – our public officers, our transport workers and those in social services, our safe distancing ambassadors, our hawkers and F&B operators, as well as our migrant workers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Most of all, I thank all Singaporeans for your strong cooperation and support – complying with our measures, coming forward to get vaccinated, trusting the Government and keeping faith with one another.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The last two years have shown us that there is nothing predictable about this virus.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But as the global pandemic enters its third year, we will have to adjust to the new normal.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We cannot let it change our hopes, our aspirations, our values.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are much stronger now compared to when the virus first emerged.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have improved our public health defences and strengthened our collective resilience.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have one of the highest vaccination rates in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And we continue to invest in and secure access to a wider range of booster and treatment options.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, as we navigate this Omicron wave and any future wave of infection, I am confident that we can overcome whatever lies ahead and make further progress in our journey to live with COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are starting the year on a positive note.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our economy has rebounded strongly from our worst recession since Independence.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The close tripartite partnership between the unions, employers and the Government enabled us to take decisive and timely actions to preserve jobs and create new ones even through the crisis.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We expect to see steady recovery this year.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Singapore will continue to benefit from the pick-up in the global economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will be supported by more widespread vaccination and booster efforts in the major economies like the US and Eurozone.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The recovery of our key trading partners in the region will also support our growth.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But that said, 2022 is not free of risks.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The global economy is still vulnerable to pandemic-related risks and further supply chain disruptions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Geopolitical and security risks loom, including the rising tensions in Eastern Europe.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We may also see a slowdown in external demand as the major economies scale back their pandemic support and central banks tighten their accommodative monetary policies to deal with the threat of inflation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to watch these potential threats.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We stand ready to respond should the situation turn for the worse.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Barring fresh disruptions, I expect the Singapore economy to continue to do well.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will support our efforts to create more good jobs and secure the livelihoods of all Singaporeans at all levels of the workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As part of this Package, I will provide a Small Business Recovery Grant for SMEs that have been most affected by COVID-19 restrictions over the past year, like those in F&B, Retail, Tourism and the Hospitality sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Local sole proprietors and partnerships in eligible sectors, as well as Singapore Food Agency (SFA) licensed hawkers, market and coffeeshop stallholders who do not hire local employees, will also receive a $1,000 payout.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In addition, workers who continue to face income loss due to COVID-19 can apply for the COVID-19 Recovery Grant, which we have extended to the end of this year.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And I will also extend the Jobs Growth Incentive by six months to September this year, with stepped-down support rates reflecting the improved labour market conditions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This extension will cover those who face greater difficulty finding jobs, like mature workers who have not been employed for six months or more, persons with disabilities and ex-offenders.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Aside from this Package, I will continue to extend targeted assistance for the aviation sector.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This includes measures to ensure public health and safety at the airport, as well as to preserve core capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must preserve and enhance our status as an international aviation hub.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Minister for Transport will share more details at the Committee of Supply (COS).

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As our economy reopens, the harder-hit sectors should progressively see improved prospects.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Meanwhile, these support measures will provide temporary relief for our businesses and workers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are also closely monitoring the risk of rising inflation and cost of living.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The rise in prices comes after an extended period of low inflation over the past decade.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It has been driven mainly by the recovery in global demand amidst continuing supply chain dislocations and especially, by the rise in energy prices.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I recognise the immediate concerns of businesses and households and will provide significant additional support in this Budget to help them tide over the current period of higher prices.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For businesses, the spike in the cost of materials and electricity has led to cashflow concerns.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is on top of the Foreign Worker Levy rebates that construction firms are receiving currently.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For households, I will introduce a Household Support Package.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will provide children below the age of 21 with a top-up of $200 each in their Child Development Account, Edusave Account or Post-Secondary Education Account.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will be on top of the annual Edusave top-ups they already receive.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will also distribute another set of $100 CDC Vouchers this year to support all Singaporean households in their daily expenses.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The vouchers can be used at participating heartland shops and hawkers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Details of the Jobs and Business Support Package, and the Household Support Package are in the Annex.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond the immediate outlook, we must set our eyes on the future.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have come this far as a nation, because we are always thinking about tomorrow: planning and taking actions not just for the present, but also with the longer-term interests of Singapore and Singaporeans at heart.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we must position ourselves now for the challenges and also the opportunities of the decade ahead.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are moving forward from a position of strength.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our responses to the pandemic have distinguished us from other countries.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have kept our air and sea ports open, and ensured an uninterrupted flow of critical supplies.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have enhanced our reputation as a trusted and reliable node.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is why we are not only attracting more investments, but also securing more high quality, cutting-edge and innovative projects.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Singapore continues to be a strategic launch pad for businesses around the world looking to expand into new markets in the region.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, BioNTech, the company that, together with Pfizer, developed the mRNA COVID-19 vaccine, is establishing its regional headquarters for Southeast Asia in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: BioNTech also plans to build a fully integrated mRNA manufacturing facility here, which will be operational as early as next year.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The new facility will boost BioNTech’s regional and global supply capacity for its growing pipeline of novel mRNA-based product candidates.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Together with other new investments and plans to build businesses and headquarter operations in Singapore, this will create many good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our ability to create jobs will depend on how quickly we restructure and transform the economy to take advantage of new opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It will also depend on us getting our foreign worker policies right.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, even as we adjust these policies, we must remain open and welcoming to talent from around the world.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: On the whole, we are making good progress.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our productivity is increasing, enabling continued income growth for our workers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are advancing as a Smart City, with our world class infrastructure and digitally-enabled workforce as our key competitive strengths.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also have a more vibrant startup and innovation ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Last year alone, 11 Singapore-based startups achieved unicorn status – no mean feat for a small city-state.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These and other technology firms create many highly-skilled jobs and opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our economic prospects are good, but we will have to contend with new external challenges and adapt quickly to a new environment.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have entered a new era of greater contestation for influence between countries and blocs, which may erode the rules-based multilateral system that has been so crucial to Singapore’s success.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In particular, rivalry between the two great powers – US and China – has intensified and will impact the world for the rest of the decade and more.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The pandemic has also turbocharged the move to a digital future.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Every time a task moves to the digital realm, it becomes easier to use software to automate and optimise it.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Such new digital technologies will disrupt and reshape businesses and impact a wide range of jobs across all sectors of the economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our local businesses, especially those that are digitally savvy, will be able to take advantage of the rich opportunities on offer and transcend our geographical limitations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But this cuts both ways, as it will also be possible for MNCs to “reshore” more functions to their home countries, as they seek to simplify and localise their supply chains.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In short, we are entering a future where conditions are more volatile, the global environment more unpredictable and change more fast-paced than ever.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We can and must adjust and still excel in this new environment.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our enterprises and workers will need to accelerate their transformation and develop new capabilities to stay ahead of the competition and look for opportunities beyond our shores and in new areas.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But there will be segments of our society who are displaced.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The fast pace of change can also give rise to a greater sense of anxiety and insecurity about the future.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is not the first time we have faced such concerns.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: When we emerged from the Global Financial Crisis of 2009 and began restructuring our economy in earnest, we were keenly aware of those who could be left behind.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we stepped up efforts to reskill and upskill our workers, and to strengthen our social security system.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We enhanced Workfare and launched the Progressive Wage Model to uplift the incomes of lower-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We introduced Silver Support to supplement the retirement income of seniors who had low incomes in their working years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We implemented MediShield Life to provide universal and lifelong protections against large hospital bills.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, these policies have become vital pillars of our social security system.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And these efforts have made our growth more inclusive.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we cannot stop here in our efforts to strengthen our social compact.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must continue to do more in a post-pandemic future, where our workers and firms will be exposed to more competition and where there will be greater churn for our businesses and livelihoods.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the coming years, we expect an increasing shift in market rewards towards those with the highest skills and those who are best able to take advantage of new technologies.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will make it harder to keep our growth inclusive and to hold our society tightly together.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Besides these growing economic and employment-related risks, there are other forces on the horizon that raise the stakes in our efforts to preserve social solidarity and will also have significant implications for our future generations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are now one of the fastest ageing countries.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ageing will mean an inexorable rise in demand for healthcare and social care.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, our means to provide for this will come under strain, as the ratio of our working population to aged dependents decreases.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must therefore plan ahead to ensure we will have the resources needed to look after more seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must also take decisive steps to join the global effort in tackling climate change.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If the world is unable to cut emissions sufficiently in time and temperatures rise beyond a certain level, we risk extreme flooding and weather events.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This could result in food and water stress for hundreds of millions of people around the world.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Island nations like Singapore will be especially threatened.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But it is a cost we cannot afford to skimp on, for it is existential.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It affects our very survival and the Singapore that our children will live in.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we must take actions now to progressively decarbonise our economy and change our way of life.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The changes brought about by the pandemic, rising geopolitical contestation, climate change, as well as domestic issues like our rapidly ageing society – these are the defining challenges of our time.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They call for robust policy responses to reinforce our resilience and retool our capabilities for the future.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: More importantly, to overcome these major tests and trials, we must continue to stand united as one.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is why it is more important than ever to renew and strengthen our social compact and to reaffirm our values and what we stand for as a nation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our existing social compact has been shaped by our history, beginning as a young and vulnerable nation thrust into independence.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We start and maintain the basic premise that no one owes us a living and that we are responsible for our own defence and survival.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The pillars underpinning our social compact – the individual, community groups, businesses and the state – all play a role, complementing one another and contributing to a system of mutual support.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The individual works hard to be self-reliant and to provide for his or her family.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Community groups, be it unions, charities or voluntary associations, come together to help different groups of people.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Employers do their part to invest in workers, advance their well-being and improve the quality of jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government creates the conditions for a vibrant economy, invests heavily in our citizens and delivers essential public services.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government, working actively with the community and tripartite partners, also provides an extra hand to those who start with less, to keep social mobility a defining feature of our society, to mitigate life’s inevitable inequalities and to provide support for the elderly.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Even with the demands of building a nation and reinvesting continually in our future, we have been able to keep public expenditures in Singapore extremely lean.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is probably the lowest among the more developed economies, yet it has produced social and economic outcomes that have been better than most.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We generate sufficient revenues to fund this expenditure and to maintain a balanced Budget.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are supported by our Net Investment Returns Contribution, or NIRC, which is a continuing stream of income from the reserves we have accumulated over the years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This means that for every dollar we spend on public services, about 80 cents is funded by tax.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The remaining 20 cents is funded through the NIRC.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This fiscal approach has enabled us to keep our overall tax burden low.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Currently, half of our workers do not have to pay personal income taxes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In particular, for the middle-income, we have deliberately ensured a low tax burden so that they can enjoy the rewards of their hard work.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Put another way, for the quality of public services we have in healthcare, education, housing, transport and many other areas, the amount of tax our citizens pay is much lower compared to many developed countries.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The continental European and Nordic countries have a different social compact, arising from their different histories.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They have much higher levels of state-financed welfare provisions, designed to meet the needs of their citizens from cradle to grave.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Their governments typically spend well above 30% of their GDP.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To fund such a spending, they impose high income taxes, usually much higher than 30%, even for the middle-income group, as well as consumption taxes that range from 20% to 25%.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We do not intend to adopt the European model of comprehensive universal welfare and high taxes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But as we tackle the challenges of a changing world, and as our own society ages and faces new stresses, we will have to do more to preserve and strengthen the unity of our people and our social compact.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, we have already been adjusting our approach over the years, with the Government progressively doing more to support the community and individuals.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The increase has gone to programmes that have made a difference in Singaporeans’ lives, like higher subsidies in our healthcare system and in tertiary education, as well as schemes like SkillsFuture, Workfare and Silver Support.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the coming decade, we will invest even more in our people and social infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will spare no effort to ensure that all Singaporeans continue to have access to world-class education and healthcare, affordable housing, good jobs and have peace of mind over their retirement needs as they grow old.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will strengthen our system of collective risk sharing, so as to give Singaporeans more assurance in managing life’s uncertainties.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We want every Singaporean to know and feel that he or she has a stake in our society – that everyone’s contributions matter and that they will not be left to fend for themselves when times are down.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We want to uphold that sense of obligation to each other and strengthen the assurance that, whatever the challenges we face, we will always have each other’s back.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They reflect the need to respond to lasting, structural shifts in our society, as well as our new social and environmental aspirations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The spending requirements will therefore be recurring in nature, not temporary.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Given this, it would not be right to dip into our reserves to meet these new needs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must husband our reserves for use in major crises and emergencies, as was necessary during the Global Financial Crisis, and especially in the last two years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must ensure that we continue to get a steady stream of income from the reserves to benefit both today’s generation of Singaporeans and our children and grandchildren.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: On the expenditure side, our needs are significant and growing.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: On the revenue side, we will not have enough to cover the additional spending needs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The stream of income from NIRC should keep pace with economic growth over time, in spite of a more challenging global investment environment.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These tax adjustments will help to raise additional revenue and also contribute to a fairer revenue structure.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That means everyone chips in and contributes to a vibrant economy and strengthened social compact, but those with greater means contribute a larger share.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, we are mindful of the impact of the tax increases on households and businesses and will have a very comprehensive set of measures to cushion the impact and help Singaporeans adjust.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This Budget therefore is about charting our new way forward together.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is a first step in renewing and strengthening our social compact for a post-pandemic world and in realising our vision of a fairer, more sustainable and more inclusive society.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Even before COVID-19, we had started to restructure our economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Through the Industry Transformation Maps, or ITMs, we have been steadily building up the capabilities we need for the future.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have also opened up new avenues of growth, by strengthening our network of Free Trade Agreements and enhancing cooperation with like-minded partners in the digital and green economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Crucially, we have a window of opportunity over the next few years to establish leading positions in key market segments.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we will accelerate our investments in new capabilities to power our next stage of growth.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our first priority is to strengthen our digital capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, we are one of the most connected cities in the world and amongst the first to roll-out a 5G standalone network.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In parallel, we have built digital utilities, like SingPass, Myinfo and PayNow, that allow our people and businesses to access digital services and transact seamlessly and safely.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The use cases for such high speeds are still nascent, but there are many new possibilities for augmented and virtual reality tools, limited only by our imagination.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: More details can be found in the Annex.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Minister for Communications and Information will also elaborate further at the COS.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second, we will push for pervasive innovation across the economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Public investments in R&D also serve as a catalyst for similar investments in the private sector.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Unfortunately, our total business expenditure on R&D still lags other economies.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Presently, most of this R&D is driven by MNCs, which have greater scale and better resources.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will therefore provide more support for our local firms to undertake R&D activities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We currently have a network of more than 80 centres across our Polytechnics and ITE engaging in technology, innovation and enterprise activities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These centres work closely with SMEs to undertake industry projects, many of which have led to new innovations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, Nanyang Polytechnic’s Automation and Robotics Innovation Centre collaborated with Sanwa-Intec Asia, an SME that supplies the automotive industry, to design and implement robotics and automation solutions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: One of the solutions is a robotic tool that emulates an operator’s handling of hot moulded products.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Previously, you would need a human operator to do the work manually.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Now, they get the job done using the robotics system.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, Sanwa-Intec has significantly raised production volume, while reducing its energy consumption.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Students from Nanyang Polytechnic also had the chance to work on these projects.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: One of them is Alysia Ong, who is now working at Sanwa-Intec after completing her internship there.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Such collaborations are a win-win – SMEs get to tap on the R&D capabilities in our Polytechnics and ITE, while students can contribute meaningfully to these projects and gain valuable hands-on industry experience.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To further support such collaborations, I will increase the capacity of the centres so that they can provide research and innovation support to more SMEs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We look forward to many more success stories in the coming years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Third, we will strengthen our local enterprise ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For the broad base of SMEs, our priority is to raise their productivity.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is more than double the number of projects supported since the scheme began.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Under this initiative, we will provide bespoke assistance tailored to the needs of promising local enterprises, in areas like innovation, internationalisation and the fostering of partnerships with other firms.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Many of these enterprises also need more support in talent development.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will launch a new Singapore Global Executive Programme, to help them to attract and nurture their next generation of leaders through industry and overseas attachments, mentorships and peer support networks.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Besides grants and bespoke assistance, some companies also need help with their financing needs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We provide such help through the Enterprise Financing Scheme.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I will enhance two components of the Scheme.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I will expand the M&A loan programme to include domestic M&A activities from 1 April this year to 31 March 2026.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will support companies to grow and expand through mergers and acquisitions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I had earlier announced the extension of the enhanced Trade Loan till September this year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Beyond this six-month extension, I will maintain the enhanced 70% risk-share under the Trade Loan for enterprises venturing into more nascent markets like Bangladesh or Brazil.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We hope this will encourage our enterprises to seek untapped opportunities in these markets.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Minister for Trade and Industry will share more about our enterprise development strategy at the COS.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I will also make further refinements to our tax schemes, to support businesses and strengthen our competitiveness and resilience.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We continue to invest significantly in education, to help every child achieve their full potential.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Through SkillsFuture, we are also empowering and equipping Singaporeans for their lifelong journey of acquiring new skills and sharpening existing ones.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To support this, we are transforming our Institutes of Higher Learning, or IHLs, which include the Autonomous Universities, into institutes for continual learning.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will review the programming in our IHLs and enhance their provision of quality continuing education and training.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Minister for Education will say more about this at the COS.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our enterprises also play a critical role in fostering a culture of lifelong learning at the workplace.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Employers are well placed to identify skills that are in demand and provide industry-relevant training.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We support employers to do so through the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Today, only employers that have had at least three local employees and contributed at least $750 of Skills Development Levy over a qualifying period, are eligible for this Credit – and these have tended to be larger enterprises.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The deadline to claim the credit will also be extended by a year, to 30 June 2024, to give employers more time to use the credit.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To maximise the investments in our people, we must also ensure a good match between the skills demanded by the industry and those offered by the workforce.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This means bringing together the various parties involved – training providers, employment facilitation providers, employers and jobseekers themselves – to anticipate the areas where new skills are required and ensure that effective training is provided in a timely manner.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: At the same time, employers need to redesign jobs to harness technology more effectively and make better use of the upgraded skills of their workers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our tripartite partners, especially the unions, help to achieve this.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: One approach that NTUC has championed and that has proved effective is the Company Training Committees, or CTCs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The CTC model brings together the unions and employers to develop concrete firm-level transformation plans, including the relevant training needed for their workers, so that they can enjoy better wages, welfare and prospects.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These plans are then implemented with the support of relevant Government agencies.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: One SME that has benefited from this partnership is Speco Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Speco started out in cleaning services and later shifted its operations to provide disinfection services through technology solutions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Building Construction and Timber Industries Employees' Union, or BATU, worked with Speco management to form a CTC and to map out the training needed to reskill its workforce.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: One beneficiary is Shamsul Nurhakim, who joined Speco on a Work-Study Programme.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Shamsul will be completing a Diploma in Applied Science from Republic Polytechnic this year, under the sponsorship of Speco.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Besides the CTCs, we will continue to extend our outreach, especially to smaller companies, through other platforms.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This includes partnering with industry leaders or Queen Bee companies to provide training and advice to smaller companies and working closely with the trade associations and chambers as well as the Singapore Business Federation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will also pay special attention to our mid-career workers, especially those in their 40s and 50s.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They are more vulnerable to churn and disruptions in the workplace.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But they have valuable experience to contribute and, with some help, many are able to learn, adapt and do well in new jobs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, Mr Manokaran was 58 years old when his job as an events manager was badly affected by the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: He decided to move to a new area and took a leap of faith into digital marketing.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Through the Career Conversion Programme for Digital Advertising Professionals, he joined an IT business solutions company and picked up new skills.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Now, he is a Digital Marketing Manager, a job with good prospects in the digital economy.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Today, we have a range of support measures to help mid-career workers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For Mr Manokaran and his employer, what worked was a place-and-train arrangement where he was first hired and then given on-the-job training by the company.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In other cases, an attach-and-train modality may be more appropriate, for example, if a company is not yet ready to commit upfront to hiring more staff.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These courses will be highly subsidised and after the training, we will provide employment facilitation services to maximise the jobseekers’ prospects.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Even as we invest in Singaporeans, we must continue to stay open and bring in manpower and skills from around the world.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: By combining local and foreign professionals, we form the best teams in Singapore to create value together.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This gives us that extra advantage to excel amidst intense global competition and to create many more good jobs and career choices for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have in place a comprehensive foreign worker policy framework to allow companies to access a diverse pool of manpower.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We continually review and adjust the key policy parameters in the framework and will introduce several changes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: First, we will update the framework for Employment Pass or EP holders.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: EP holders should be professionals and senior executives who can contribute to our economy, sharpen the skills of those they work with, and strengthen our workforce.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To ensure that EP holders are of the right calibre, we adjust the minimum qualifying salary from time to time – because how much the employer is prepared to pay is a practical indicator of the quality of the EP holder.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For the financial services sector, which has higher salary norms, this will be raised from the current $5,000 to $5,500.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The qualifying salaries for older EP applicants, which increase progressively with age, will also be raised in tandem.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For renewal applications, these changes will apply from September next year to give businesses sufficient time to adjust.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Beyond the qualifying salary, we will refine how we assess EP applications, to improve the complementarity and diversity of our foreign workforce, and also to increase certainty and transparency for businesses.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Likewise, for S Pass holders, we have a minimum qualifying salary to ensure that those coming in are of the right quality.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will aim for the S Pass holders to be comparable in quality to the top one-third of local Associate Professionals and Technicians.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Similar to the EP framework, we will increase the qualifying salary for S Pass holders to achieve this and we will do so in phases.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And the qualifying salaries for older S Pass holders will be raised in tandem.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Thereafter, the minimum qualifying salary for new S Pass applicants will be raised in September next year and, again, in September 2025.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The specific salary values will be announced closer to the implementation date, based on the prevailing local wages then.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And similar to EP, the changes will apply to renewal applications one year later, to give businesses time to adjust.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In addition, we currently regulate the number of S Pass holders with sub-Dependency Ratio Ceilings and levies.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will help transform the sectors that have been more heavily dependent on foreign workers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Minister for Manpower will elaborate further on the foreign worker policy changes at the COS.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The adjustments in our foreign worker policies apply mainly to the broad middle of the workforce.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is where we have Singaporeans doing the jobs, but we need to continually adjust our rules to ensure better complementarity between our foreign and local workforce.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: At the higher end of the workforce, where there are acute skill shortages, we will continue to bring in professionals with the right abilities to be part of Team Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Ultimately, our investments to develop stronger capabilities across our businesses and workforce reflect our mindset of continuous improvement.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We must always strive to do better and achieve more.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will put us in good stead to meet the challenges of the future.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Climate change is a global crisis that becomes more pressing with each passing year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: At last year’s UN Climate Change Conference in Glasgow (COP26), countries were urged to get to net zero emissions by or around the middle of the century, to keep alive the ambition of limiting global warming to 1.5 degrees celsius above pre-industrial levels.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But unless deep reductions in CO2 and other greenhouse gas emissions occur in the coming decades, global warming will exceed 1.5 degrees, or even two degrees in this century.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, the world needs to take urgent action.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Singapore is fully committed to doing our part in the global movement to tackle climate change.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But, unlike many other countries, we are highly disadvantaged by a lack of natural renewable energy sources.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We do not have huge rivers or hot springs to draw hydro or geothermal power.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We do not have the land for wind or solar energy to be sufficient for our own needs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But thankfully, green technologies have been improving by leaps and bounds.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Alternative low-carbon solutions, like carbon capture, utilisation and storage, and hydrogen, are starting to look more plausible.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: At COP26, Singapore helped to finalise a landmark decision on Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, which unlocks the door for carbon credits to be traded on a global basis.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Such developments give us greater confidence to review our long-term climate goals.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Two years ago, we made an international commitment to peak our emissions around 2030.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And we also announced our Long-Term Low-Emissions Development Strategy, or LEDS, to halve our emissions from its peak by 2050 and to achieve net zero emissions as soon as viable in the second half of the century.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are on track to achieving our 2030 target.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: With advances in technology and new opportunities for international collaboration in areas like carbon markets, we believe we can bring forward our net zero timeline.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will therefore raise our ambition to achieve net zero emissions by or around mid-century.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will consult closely with industry and citizen stakeholder groups to firm up and finalise our plans before making a formal revision of our LEDS later this year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To achieve this net zero ambition, we will need to set the right price of carbon, so that businesses and individuals will be able to internalise the costs of carbon and take actions to moderate their emissions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: When we introduced the carbon tax in 2019, we kept the initial tax low – at $5 per tonne of emissions – to give our businesses time to adjust.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And we are pacing the increases to the carbon tax between now and 2030, and will announce subsequent increases ahead of time.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Besides this, we will not impose an additional carbon tax on the use of petrol, diesel and compressed natural gas.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These already have excise duties that encourage users to moderate their fuel consumption and hence emissions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will continue to review and adjust these fuel excise duties periodically.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I appreciate that some businesses and households may require support as they adjust to the carbon tax increase.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, we are mindful that firms in our emissions-intensive and trade-exposed sectors may face higher costs than those in countries with lower or no carbon tax.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Such transition frameworks are found in many countries with carbon taxes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They provide existing companies with allowances for a share of their emissions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For our framework, the allowances will be determined based on efficiency standards and decarbonisation targets.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will help mitigate the impact on business costs, while still encouraging decarbonisation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will continue to engage affected companies on the design of the framework prior to its implementation in 2024.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It will also help create local demand for high-quality carbon credits and catalyse the development of well-functioning and regulated carbon markets.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will also do more to support companies, especially SMEs, to invest in energy-efficient equipment and decarbonisation solutions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For households, the higher carbon tax will be felt mainly through an increase in utility bills.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will provide support, such as additional U-Save rebates, to help cushion the impact during the transition.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: More details will be announced next year, ahead of the carbon tax increase in 2024.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I should clarify that I do not expect to derive additional revenue from this increase in the carbon tax.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Some of the revenue will be used to cushion the impact on households and businesses.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: A large part of the revenue will be used to support a decisive shift towards decarbonisation through investments in new low-carbon and more energy efficient solutions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These investments will help to lower our emissions and bring us closer towards our net zero goal.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The path towards net zero will entail significant economic restructuring and changes in how we live and work in the future.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: All of us – the public, businesses, the Government – will face difficult choices.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Costly investments may be required, for example, to import or generate low-carbon energy.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But now is the time when we must move decisively towards the future of a net zero world.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will allow us to tap fully on the many exciting possibilities in this green transition.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And that is why we launched the Singapore Green Plan 2030 last year, to bring everyone on board our sustainability movement.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Over the coming decade, we expect to see a “greening” of traditional sectors of our economy, like aviation, energy and tourism.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: At the same time, emerging green sectors like green finance and carbon services will grow in prominence.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Millions of new green jobs will be created around the world and demand for talent with green skills will increase.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Moving quickly will position Singapore to build on our competitive advantages to capture these opportunities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We can become the go-to location in Asia for expertise in carbon services and the trusted regional marketplace for carbon credits.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As a key node for international air and sea transport networks, we can become a frontrunner in the development of sustainable aviation and marine fuels.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In the financial services sector, for example, green finance is one of the fastest growing segments.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Singapore now accounts for close to half of the ASEAN green bond and loan market.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We aim to do more, so that banks and financial institutions will use Singapore as a base to develop their capabilities and to develop innovative green financial solutions to service their customers all over Asia and the world.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will include bonds issued by the Government, as well as Statutory Boards.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Green finance is just one of many exciting new areas of green growth.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As I mentioned just now, there are many more such opportunities across every sector of the economy.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We aim to move Singapore into the forefront of green technologies – where new innovations are developed, trialled, scaled-up and eventually exported to the rest of the world.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will work hard to grab first-mover advantage and develop new engines of growth in the green economy.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Another important pillar of the Singapore Green Plan is to transform our living environment, make it a greener and more sustainable home, and a beautiful city in nature for all to enjoy.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And one aspect we have been focusing on is transport.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We aim to be a car-lite city, supported by a comprehensive public transport network, which is the cleanest and most energy-efficient mode of transport.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And this is why we are maintaining our policy of zero growth rate for private vehicles.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are perhaps the only city in the world which has taken this bold step.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For passenger vehicles, the most promising clean energy option is electric vehicles or EVs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have provided significant incentives for EV adoption.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To do this, infrastructure upgrades will be necessary and the financing can come from green bonds.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Various Ministers will elaborate more on our efforts under the Singapore Green Plan at the COS, because this is truly a whole-of-Government effort.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In advancing our green transition, we will strive to be a bright green spark and to secure a more sustainable future for ourselves and for the world.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And we are continually evolving our policies, as circumstances change, to achieve these goals.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In our earlier decades, we had three pillars in our social security system: (a)	subsidised public housing through HDB to make home ownership a reality for the vast majority of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: (b)	the CPF to help every working Singaporean save in order to own a home and build a nest-egg for retirement.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: (c)	the 3Ms of MediSave, MediShield and MediFund, together with Government subsidies, to provide Singaporeans with affordable and quality healthcare.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Over the years, we have strengthened these pillars.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We enhanced the CPF so that members with lower balances can benefit from extra interest on their retirement savings.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In public housing, we are not just helping Singaporeans own a home, but also upgrading older flats and rejuvenating estates.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In healthcare, we have gone beyond the original 3Ms.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We introduced MediShield Life to provide life-long universal insurance for hospital bills.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And as elderly care needs grew, we introduced CareShield Life and ElderFund to support our seniors.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: First, we put in place ComCare to help people through temporary difficulties and get support while they are being trained for new jobs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Second, we implemented Workfare to uplift our lower-wage workers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To complement Workfare, we introduced Silver Support to provide an additional plank of support for seniors with limited lifetime earnings.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Besides these five pillars of social support, we have invested more heavily in education as a social leveller and a source of opportunity for every Singaporean.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In recent years, we have been investing more, not just in the formal years of schooling, but also through life – starting with KidSTART, preschool and extending through adulthood through SkillsFuture.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Over the past year, we have engaged around 6,000 participants in our Conversations on Singapore Women’s Development.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Many good ideas have come up, from better support for caregivers, to stronger measures against workplace discrimination.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: When the plans are ready, the Government will commit resources and work with our partners to realise them.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we have been doing more to strengthen our social compact over the years and across many fronts.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But as new stresses emerge and as we enter a more volatile and unpredictable environment, we will take further decisive steps to strengthen the architecture of social security and opportunity for all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our healthcare needs, in particular, will grow as our population ages.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will need to help revamp our healthcare ecosystem to cater to more geriatric needs across various care settings.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Healthcare will therefore be the major driver of increased social spending in the coming decade.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In every area of spending, however, it is not just a matter of spending more, but also how we spend – to achieve the right outcomes and to preserve the values of individual responsibility and mutual support from the community, even as the Government steps in to do more.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are studying them systematically in an effort to renew and strengthen our social compact for a post-pandemic world.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will start with a few major moves in this Budget, which I will explain in turn.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: First, we will do more to uplift lower-wage workers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will also extend it to in-house cleaners, security officers, landscape workers, administrators and drivers across all sectors.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will also launch a Progressive Wage Mark or PW Mark to accredit firms that pay Progressive Wages and the Local Qualifying Salary.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: All of us – businesses, consumers and taxpayers – will have to do our part and contribute to uplifting our lower-wage workers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I recognise that some firms may need time to adjust to these changes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Some have locked in long-term contracts based on certain wage assumptions and now face higher manpower costs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will also provide some support for workers earning above $2,500 and up to $3,000, at a lower co-funding ratio.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will provide certainty of funding for the wage increases over the next five years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To complement the moves on Progressive Wages, I will also significantly enhance the Workfare Income Supplement.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will give a further boost to our lower-wage workers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This means more workers will get to benefit from Workfare.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I will introduce a minimum income criterion for Workfare at $500 per month to encourage part-timers and casual workers to take up regular, full-time work.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I will extend Workfare to younger workers aged 30 to 34 so that they can start saving for housing and retirement earlier in their careers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They will receive a maximum annual payout of $2,100.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Those aged 35 to 44 will receive a maximum annual payout of $3,000; those aged 45 to 59 will receive a maximum annual payout of $3,600.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Those aged 60 and above will receive the highest maximum payout tier of $4,200 annually.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And I will extend this same maximum payout tier to all persons with disabilities, regardless of their age.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The enhanced Workfare is expected to benefit more than half a million workers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our moves on Progressive Wages will cover around 94% of our full-time lower-wage workers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The enhanced Workfare will provide further support to all eligible Singaporean lower-wage workers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, through the combination of Progressive Wages and Workfare, we expect the incomes of our lower-wage workers to grow faster than the median wage growth over the coming decade.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, as our economy grows and society progresses, we will reduce income disparities in our workforce.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is a significant increase and it reflects our shared commitment to uplift our lower-wage workers in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Next, we will enhance the retirement adequacy of Singaporeans, especially for senior workers who are preparing for retirement.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Following the recommendations of the Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers, we will continue to increase the employer and employee CPF contribution rates for workers aged 55 to 70.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We implemented the first increase this year and have been providing employers with a one-year CPF Transition Offset equivalent to half of the increase in employer CPF contributions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will continue with the next step of the increase in 2023, and provide employers with a similar offset.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This means that workers aged 55 to 70 will see a total increase of three- to four-percentage points in their CPF contribution rates over these two years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Additionally, with rising standards of living, we will adjust the CPF Basic Retirement Sum, or BRS, to provide members with higher monthly CPF payouts in their retirement years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will raise the BRS by 3.5% per year for the next five cohorts turning 55 from 2023 to 2027.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There is no requirement for members to top up their CPF if they are unable to set aside their BRS.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Those who set aside the BRS when they turn 55 in 2027 will receive payouts of close to $1,000 per month when they are 65, and these payouts will continue for the rest of their lives.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will give them greater assurance for their basic retirement needs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Just as we uplift our vulnerable groups, we will also continue to enhance social mobility.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Government is committed to ensuring that all Singaporeans have the opportunities to do well for themselves, no matter their background or starting points.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is why we continue to invest heavily in our children to give every Singaporean child the best possible start in life.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are now doing more upstream – starting with preschool years to provide additional support for children from low-income families.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Yet, we know that some vulnerable children fall out of or behind in our education system because of difficult conditions at home.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Early intervention in their formative years can make a big difference in their lives.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: One important intervention is to provide these children with a more conducive living environment to grow up in.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For second-timer low-income families, we have the Fresh Start Housing Scheme to help them purchase a home of their own.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will enhance the scheme to better support families in their journey towards home ownership.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And the Minister for National Development will share more at the COS.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Another effective intervention is the KidSTART programme, which taps on a network of community partners to provide upstream support for eligible families with young children.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Under KidSTART, parents and caregivers are guided to support their child’s development at home, in the community and in preschools.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Thereafter, we will scale up nationwide progressively to support even more eligible families.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To complement KidSTART, we started an UPLIFT Community Pilot to strengthen support for school-going children in disadvantaged families.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This includes connecting them with social service agencies and befrienders who check in with them regularly and provide mentorship.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As our agencies develop more schemes to help different segments, there is a need for closer coordination and integration across these different services.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The challenges faced by lower-income families are often multi-faceted and inter-connected.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, a child could be absent from school because of employment or health issues faced by his or her parents.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In such cases, it is not enough to provide financial assistance.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We also need to address the underlying issues faced by the family and support them in taking steps to achieve sustainable change.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This involves taking a family-centred approach to address each family’s challenges so that they can keep their family situations stable, become self-reliant and eventually achieve social mobility.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will partner each ComLink family to develop an action plan that is customised to address their specific needs and aspirations.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Each family will have dedicated and trained befrienders to support them towards achieving their action plans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These befrienders will be the bridge with other community partners and Government agencies so that families can receive timely and holistic support.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Minister for Social and Family Development will share more about this at the COS.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have made heavy investments in healthcare over the years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, we have added five new polyclinics and doubled the number of beds in community hospitals in the last decade.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To encourage ageing in place, we have injected a significant supply of aged care services, especially in home and community care.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have improved the quality of care while keeping our healthcare affordable and accessible for all.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have achieved better overall healthcare outcomes, with Singaporeans living longer and healthier lives.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As one of the fastest-ageing nations in the world, our healthcare costs will increase significantly.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Government can and must spend more on healthcare for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But the current trajectory of increase is not sustainable.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We therefore need to fundamentally rethink the way we deliver healthcare.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: An important aspect of this is to bring care closer and make it more accessible to the community.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: A strong primary care sector will serve as the bedrock of our healthcare system and allow us to go upstream for preventive care and better manage chronic conditions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This can improve our quality of life and reduce the risk of costly downstream complications.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It will also enable our hospitals to focus on complex conditions and emergency cases.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our healthcare ecosystem must therefore be restructured over the longer term to centre the healthcare system around the patient.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It must be designed to keep patients healthy and provide care in the most appropriate setting.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, patients with diabetes will require dietary and lifestyle changes to manage the condition well.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These are best coordinated by a trusted primary care doctor.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, to do all these, we will need to build closer partnerships between our healthcare clusters and community partners, especially with the GPs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It will entail a review of our resourcing approach and healthcare financing schemes, as well as the need for more upstream investments in preventive healthcare.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will be a challenging long-term effort involving many components and stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But if we succeed, we will be able to use our resources more effectively while providing quality care and enabling Singaporeans to stay healthy.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Another aspect of healthcare that has been brought to the fore during the pandemic is mental health.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The pandemic has been a stressful period for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But the issues of mental health that we face are not caused only by COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Beyond healthcare, we have, over the last decade, made progress in ensuring that Persons with Disabilities, or PwDs, lead dignified lives and are empowered to fulfil their potential across different life stages.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We supported them through their early and schooling years with Early Intervention programmes and Special Education schools.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We built inclusive playgrounds across the island so that children with special needs can play with their peers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Through SG Enable, the employment of PwDs has increased and workplaces have been made more inclusive to cater for the needs of PwDs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will continue to do more for this group.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The community plays a critical role in building a caring and inclusive home.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Through the course of the pandemic, we have seen an outpouring of generosity, kindness and support from Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Donations received at Giving.sg, an online donation portal, last year increased by nearly threefold to around $100 million.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I will build on this momentum to strengthen the culture of giving in our society.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Charities can apply to receive dollar-for-dollar matching for eligible donations, up to a cap of $250,000 per charity every year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Earlier we had established the Community Capability Trust, to strengthen the capabilities of Social Service Agencies.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I will therefore provide a top-up of $26 million to the Charities Capability Fund for five years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will help to nurture a more productive and innovative charity sector and enable them to do more for the community.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I will also continue to support our Arts and Sports sectors.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Arts and sports provide meaningful outlets for self-expression and discovery.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They help to strengthen our shared culture and our sense of identity, and they unite us as one people.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Last year, all of us cheered our Olympians and Paralympians as they flew the Singapore flag high in Tokyo.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To strengthen our High Performance Sports ecosystem, I will extend the One Team Singapore Fund for another five years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will provide dollar-for-dollar matching for donations to rally support for our Team Singapore athletes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will continually review every aspect of our social policies to see what needs to be further adjusted and improved.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is a major multi-year agenda, to strengthen our solidarity with one another, as we prepare Singapore for the next bound.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I will therefore make major enhancements to strengthen our tax structure.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our corporate tax system will need to be updated due to global tax developments relating to the Base Erosion and Profit Shifting initiative, or BEPS 2.0.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Pillar 1 re-allocates the profit of the largest and most profitable Multinational Enterprises, or MNEs, from where activities are conducted to where consumers are located.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There are ongoing international discussions on how to determine the jurisdictions which will surrender profits for re-allocation to the markets under Pillar 1 and how much each will have to surrender.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Given our small domestic market and the extent of activities conducted here by MNEs, Singapore will lose tax revenue under Pillar 1.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: What this means is that if such an MNE were to have an effective tax rate of less than 15% in Singapore at the group level, other jurisdictions such as its home jurisdiction can collect the difference up to 15%.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The METR will top up the MNE group’s effective tax rate in Singapore to 15%.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: IRAS will study this further and consult the industry on the design of METR.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will also continue to closely monitor international developments before making any decisions on the METR.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: At this stage, it is premature and difficult to determine the eventual fiscal impact of both pillars.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As I mentioned just now, there will be a negative revenue impact under Pillar 1.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: METR might yield some additional tax revenue in the short term, but the eventual impact of Pillar 2 on our revenue will depend on how governments and companies respond.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The net impact of both Pillars depends on the rules and details, which are still being developed by the Inclusive Framework on BEPS.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: While BEPS 2.0 may have reduced the scope for tax competition, it has not reduced global competition for investments.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In fact, competition is likely to intensify as governments worldwide seek to restore and rebuild their economies after the effects of the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, there may be less tax competition but there will be other forms of competition.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will have to take this into consideration and ensure that Singapore remains one of the best places in the world for business.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will, therefore, need more time to study these issues thoroughly and will announce changes in the corporate tax system when we are ready.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is an important part of the tax system.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Apart from generating revenue, they also help to recirculate a portion of the wealth stock into our economy and in so doing, mitigate social inequalities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Wealth taxes are therefore needed to build a fairer society where everyone can aspire to succeed regardless of their backgrounds.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Currently, we tax wealth in several ways – through property tax, stamp duties and the Additional Registration Fee or ARF for motor vehicles.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, the higher value the residential property or motor vehicle, the higher the tax rate.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Ideally, we would want to tax the net wealth of individuals.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But such a tax is not easy to implement effectively.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Estimating wealth accurately and fairly is a more complex exercise than estimating incomes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Further, many forms of wealth are mobile and as long as there are differences in wealth taxes across jurisdictions, such wealth can and will move.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Singapore is not alone in facing such challenges.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Countries like Germany, France and Denmark have stopped levying taxes on individuals’ net wealth.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The number of OECD countries that levy net wealth taxes has dropped from 12 in 1990 to only three in 2020.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And this is partly because of the difficulties in effectively implementing net wealth taxes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will continue to study the experiences of other countries and explore options to tax wealth effectively.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In the meantime, we will strengthen our current system of taxes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In particular, I will make several adjustments to property tax, which is currently our principal means of taxing wealth.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
