text: I will increase the property tax rates for non-owner-occupied residential properties, which includes investment properties.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: All non-owner-occupied residential properties will face higher property taxes and the increase will be more significant for properties at the high end.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: With these changes, a large non-owner-occupied detached house in the central area with Annual Value of $150,000 will see an annual property tax bill of about $43,000 per year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This increase will impact the top 7% of owner-occupied residential properties.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The increase will be higher for properties at the top end.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To illustrate with the same landed property with Annual Value of $150,000, if this is owner-occupied, the new property tax bill will be about $28,000 a year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The increases in property tax rates will be implemented in two steps, starting with the tax payable in 2023.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: When fully implemented, they will raise our property tax revenue by about $380 million per year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I will also tax luxury cars at a higher rate to make our vehicle tax system more progressive.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I will introduce an additional ARF tier for cars at a rate of 220% for the portion of Open Market Value in excess of $80,000.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The new rates will apply to all cars registered with COEs obtained from the second COE bidding round this month.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The additional ARF is expected to generate an additional $50 million in revenue per year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The revenue from the increase in GST will go towards supporting our healthcare expenditure and to take care of our seniors.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In fact, the GST revenue by itself will not be sufficient to cover our additional healthcare spending.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Further, as I shared earlier, other areas of social spending are rising too.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And this is why we need not only the GST increase but also the changes to personal income tax, property tax and vehicle tax which I have just announced.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Where the timing of GST is concerned, I have carefully considered the overall situation – the ongoing pandemic, the state of our economy and the outlook for inflation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But I also understand the concerns that Singaporeans have about the GST increase taking place at the same time as rising prices.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I have therefore decided to delay the GST increase to 2023 and stagger the increase over two steps.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I want to assure all Singaporeans that we will continue to implement the GST in our unique Singaporean way, with features and schemes that support the less well-off.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will apply to license fees, as well as fees charged by Government agencies for the provision of services.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This includes school fees, ITE and Polytechnic fees, and charges in public carparks.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Committee will be chaired by Minister of State for Trade and Industry Ms Low Yen Ling.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The enhanced Assurance Package will provide significant payouts to Singaporeans over the next five years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Every adult Singaporean will receive cash payouts totalling $700 to $1,600.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Eligible seniors will receive a special GSTV – Cash (Seniors’ Bonus) totalling $600 to $900.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Eligible HDB households will receive additional U-Save rebates totalling $330 to $570 depending on flat type.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: All Singaporean children and seniors will receive MediSave top-ups totalling $450.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: All Singaporean households will receive two tranches of CDC vouchers worth $200 each in 2023 and 2024.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The vouchers can be used at all participating heartland merchants and hawkers, as well as major supermarkets.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For the majority of Singaporean households, the offsets from the Assurance Package will cover at least five years of additional GST expenses.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For lower-income households, they will receive more – with offsets covering about 10 years’ worth of additional GST expenses.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, take a middle-income family of four in a 4-room flat, with two school-going children and a household income of about $8,000 a month.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They will receive a total of around $4,000 in benefits, around five times the additional GST they are expected to incur a year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If I were to choose a lower-income family, the benefits they receive will be larger and the offsets will cover more years of additional GST expenses.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Take the example of a retired couple in a 3-room flat.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They will receive even more support from the Assurance Package, at around $6,800.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This far exceeds 10 times the additional GST they are expected to incur a year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Even with these offsets, some vulnerable households may require more support.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These households with urgent needs can approach their Citizens’ Consultative Committees (CCC) for assistance.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To further support vulnerable households, I will top up the CCC ComCare Fund by $5 million over five years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I will also provide a total of $12 million over four years to our Self-Help Groups.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In addition, businesses may need to adjust to the GST increase.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, I will set aside close to $40 million under the Productivity Solutions Grant for businesses to apply for subsidised accounting and point of sale solutions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Over and above the transitional support provided by the Assurance Package, I will enhance the GST Voucher or GSTV scheme which is a permanent feature of our system.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The permanent GSTV scheme currently has three components – a cash payout, MediSave top-up and utilities rebates.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: First, the Service and Conservancy Charges (S&CC) Rebate will be made a permanent component of the GSTV scheme.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The enhanced permanent GSTV scheme will provide continuing offsets for the GST expenses of lower-to middle-income households, and most retiree households, beyond the transitional period covered by the Assurance Package.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The enhanced GSTV will fully offset the total GST that retiree households living in 1- to 4-room HDB flats have to pay.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Many retiree households in bigger flats will also have their GST offset by a significant amount.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For low-income households who do not have elderly members, the GSTV will offset about half their total GST expenses every year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Both the Assurance Package and the enhanced permanent GSTV scheme will be implemented together, before the GST rate increase, so that Singaporeans can benefit from both schemes at the same time.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Low-income households, in particular, will be well looked after.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Besides the offsets in the Assurance Package, the permanent GSTV ensures that they will receive significant support on a continuing basis.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is why the GST increase will not hurt low-income households.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For them, the impact of the increase in GST will be neutralised.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Budget supports spending on programmes for all, in areas like security, housing, education, health.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Every dollar collected flows back to our taxpayers in one way or another.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The benefits show up in many ways: in our seniors’ Silver Support payments; in our lower-wage workers’ Workfare payouts; in the subsidies for our loved ones for healthcare; in the childcare subsidies that parents enjoy; in the quality education every child receives.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are reminded of them every day when we look around – our roads, MRT lines, hospitals, schools, the beautiful parks.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In the safety and security our families enjoy.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But when it comes to paying for these benefits, we should not shirk from our responsibilities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Ultimately, every need must be paid by someone – every dollar not paid by one person will have to be made up by someone else, either today or in the future.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But what we can and will always do is to ensure that we have a fair and progressive system in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This means that those with more will contribute more taxes than the benefits they receive.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Those with less will still contribute, but a lesser amount and they will receive more benefits in return.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This reflects our values and who we are as a society.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is how we strengthen our social compact.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is how we will fund our common aspirations for tomorrow.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is the result of our swift and decisive response, which allowed us to avert worse public health outcomes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We saw a stronger-than-expected rebound in our economy and businesses, and did not need to utilise measures like loan loss provisions which we had set aside.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is mainly due to a reduced expenditure of $10 billion for the COVID-19 Resilience Package, underutilisation of Ministries’ expenditures primarily due to projects delayed by COVID-19, as well as one-off revenue upsides, including from Vehicle Quota Premiums and stamp duties.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We also tapped on our existing resources first to provide short-term relief when we had to tighten restrictions periodically last year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, the $2 billion worth of economic relief measures introduced during the Heightened Alerts last year was resourced through a re-allocation of funds.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: During the Stabilisation Phase, we introduced $1.4 billion worth of support measures.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For timely implementation of these measures, we took an advance from the Contingencies Fund.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I will now replace the advances through the Supplementary Budget for FY2021.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For FY2022, we will set aside $6 billion to maintain a multi-layered public health defence.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is necessary for us to respond nimbly and confidently to the evolving COVID-19 situation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Given the extraordinary nature of this pandemic, we will resource this COVID-19 public health expenditure for FY2022 from Past Reserves.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This cumulative draw is less than the initial draw of $52 billion that the President had originally agreed to for FY2020.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It reflects our prudence in the use of Past Reserves.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Beyond the crisis, our spending needs will continue to grow, as we tackle structural shifts and invest more to deliver on our longer-term priorities as I had laid out just now in this Budget.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In order to meet new spending needs, besides raising revenue, we will continue to manage our expenditure growth.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Since FY2017, we have implemented a 2% cut in the budgets of all Ministries and Organs of State to ensure we spend judiciously and achieve good value-for-money outcomes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Funds from this adjustment will be channelled towards new priorities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For FY2021, I expect an overall deficit of $5 billion or 0.9% of GDP.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Life has not been perfect; we have stumbled and struggled, here and there.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But all things told, we can be very proud of where we are today.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Remember we were once thought to be an improbable nation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are a little red dot; a most unlikely country.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are the only city in the world with a military and foreign service.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are a diverse city in one of the most highly diverse regions in the world.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are the only city of this size that is also a country and a hub for the world.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Throughout our nation’s history, we have faced many crises.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our Pioneers still remember what it was like during the Japanese Occupation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: World War II seems very distant to us.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But for the survivors, the experiences left them with indelible lessons.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There is an exhibition now at the National Museum marking the 80th anniversary of the fall of Singapore, with stories of those who lived through it.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: One of them is Mdm Sim Soo Wee.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: She was just seven years old when she lost her parents during the Occupation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: She still remembers vividly the hardships of war, and how she and the people around her persevered through the most difficult days and she said: “I hope that the younger generation will continue to stay united and demonstrate the same fortitude and resilience in the face of their own tests”.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Indeed, over the subsequent decades, we have confronted many other challenges We had the communist insurgency in the 1950s.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We went through the tumultuous period of the 1960s and early 1970s, with racial riots, separation from Malaysia and the sudden departure of the British.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Since then, we have had to deal with one crisis after another – economic recessions, 9/11 and terrorism, SARS and the Global Financial Crisis.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Through these crucibles of fire, we forged our Singapore spirit – a spirit that is resolute and indomitable; that never gives up, and never says die.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Instead, it has strengthened our steel, deepened our bonds and brought us closer together as one united people.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And so, it has been in the last two years of the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have made many sacrifices, stood together and measured up as one people.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They remind us that we are stronger when we stand together.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I was especially cheered by the responses of our youth throughout this pandemic.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They have taken the restrictions in their stride and found new ways to learn online, and to keep in touch with their friends.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Lions fought hard and gave it their all.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I am sure all of us will have our own memories of how the Singapore spirit shone brilliantly in the darkest hours of the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Let us draw strength from these experiences and continue to keep faith with one another.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There will be unexpected problems ahead, as there were in the past.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They have to be met, grappled with and resolved.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But looking back at what we have been through during these COVID-19 years, we have nothing to fear.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will always prevail, so long as we continue to stand side by side in solidarity with one another, regardless of race, language, or religion.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will chart a new way forward together.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will see through the pandemic today and build a better Singapore tomorrow.
